html:
SMTO-EXE-0238 — What you approved changed before SMTO could act on it

GUID: 9d442f20-f4c1-50d0-ac72-7e6ab4d853e4
Slug: docker-destructive-scope-changed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • SMTO stopped because the thing you approved changed before Docker started the work: the cleanup selection, the Compose project files, or a file in the build folder. Nothing was deleted or changed by this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you or a program are editing the Compose files or the build folder on the Gateway, finish and save those edits first. SMTO refuses to act when files change between your review and the start of the work.
  2. Ask SMTO to read the Compose project again, or to make a new cleanup preview, and review what it shows. The new review captures the current files or items, so the next request matches what you approve.
  3. When asking for a cleanup, ask for exactly the kinds of items shown in the preview, and only remove a volume that appears in that preview. A cleanup that asks for anything different from the preview is refused to protect your data.
  4. Approve the new request. Once the reviewed version and the current state match, the work can go ahead safely.

What success looks like

  • The Compose change, build or cleanup completes and SMTO reports success for the new request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer, noting whether you were editing files at the time. Don't change the project files while SMTO is building or starting the project.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused the Docker operation because its scope no longer matched what was reviewed: prune categories or the chosen volume differed from the preview, the Compose configuration revision changed, or a build-context file changed while being packaged.

What this means

  • Requested deletion categories/volume differed from the preview, Compose configuration changed from its accepted revision or a build-context file changed identity/size during archive construction. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Requested deletion categories/volume differed from the preview, Compose configuration changed from its accepted revision or a build-context file changed identity/size during archive construction.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the mismatch concerns prune scope, Compose revision or build-file identity before refreshing the relevant evidence.

How to fix it

  • For prune, request a new preview and submit exactly its categories (and a volume listed among its candidates). For Compose, re-run docker.compose_config and pass the new revision as expected_revision. For builds, stop processes writing into context_path and retry once its files are stable.
  • Refresh and review the affected prune preview, Compose configuration or build context before new mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Obtain a new preview or resolved Compose revision and confirm the exact changed scope.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact reviewed scope and source revisions remain consistent through the intended operation.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
